title: Easter Sunday vigil held for 16-year-old girl killed in officer-involved shooting
article: A vigil and solidarity action was held on Easter Sunday for a 16-year-old girl who died as a result of an officer-involved shooting on Wednesday.

The family and friends of Eishia Hudson gathered at the intersection of Lagimodiere and Fermor Avenue, for the vigil, which was announced in a posting Saturday on the Facebook page Justice for Eishia Car Vigil, hosted by Winnipeg Police Cause Harm. Attendees were asked to remain in their vehicles or keep a two arms length distance away from other participants to maintain social distancing.
For those unable to attend to show support in-person, comments on the Facebook event were opened to post songs, messages, and pictures of support using #JusticeForEishia, according to the post.

The intersection was closed down for several hours by Winnipeg Police for the vigil. "Lagimodiere and Fermor is an 80 km/h speed zone and it is our duty to ensure the safety of all individuals who wished to attend," the Winnipeg Police Service tweeted Sunday night. "The intersection was closed in the same regard we would any other intersection."

On Thursday, Winnipeg Police announced that a 16-year-old girl had been fatally shot at Lagimodiere and Fermor following a pursuit of a suspected stolen vehicle. Police said the five teenaged occupants of the vehicle were believed to have taken part in a robbery at the Sage Creek Liquor Mart earlier that evening. Officers subsequently provided medical treatment to the female driver, and she was taken to hospital in critical condition but was pronounced dead police said. She was later identified by her family.
Police said the four other occupants were charged with robbery and other offences and detained in custody.
The Independent Investigation Unit of Manitoba (IIU) has taken over responsibility of the investigation into the police-involved shooting.
A gofundme page has been set up to help Hudson\'s family cover funeral costs with over $9,000 raised as of Monday.
